about.title: Pinole Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Pinole's location along I-80, with San Pablo Avenue running through the heart of town, means residents deal with steady traffic and, at times, collisions that leave people hurt and unsure what comes next. Recent public records show dozens of injury crashes each year in this Contra Costa County city, with Wednesday evening hours between 5 and 7 p.m. showing up frequently in the data. If you were injured in one of these crashes, the period right after matters — insurers move fast, and evidence like skid marks, dashcam footage, or witness memories fade quickly. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we're a free service that connects injured Pinole residents with independent attorneys who work on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. Getting matched with someone who understands local roads like I-80 and San Pablo Avenue can help you avoid early missteps with insurance adjusters.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Talking to the Insurer

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock Is Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident lawsuit in California, but if a government vehicle or road defect was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. An attorney can spot these deadlines early and make sure paperwork isn't missed.

items.title: Comparative Fault Means Partial Blame Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're partly responsible for a Pinole crash, you can still recover a reduced amount. Insurers sometimes use this rule to minimize payouts, which is why having someone review the facts on your side matters.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering, But Insurers Will Test You
items.desc: California doesn't limit non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases, yet adjusters often try to get injured people to downplay their injuries in a recorded statement. Speaking with an attorney before giving any statement can protect the value of your claim.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally wise to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim later. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: I was hurt in a crash on I-80 near Pinole — does it matter if it happened on the eastbound or westbound side?
items.answer: The direction of travel itself doesn't change your legal rights, but it can affect which agency or jurisdiction handled the collision report and which evidence is available. An attorney familiar with local corridors like I-80 and San Pablo Avenue can help track down the right records for your specific crash.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a Pinole car accident?
items.answer: In most car accident cases in California, you have two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. That window can be much shorter if a government entity, like a public road crew or transit vehicle, was involved. Because deadlines vary by situation, it's best to have an attorney review your specific facts as soon as possible.
